title: Purchase order
description: One purchase order to a supplier, at supply-chain/purchase-orders/<id>.json (route supply-chain/purchase-orders/[id]), following APQC PCF 4.2.3 (order materials and services). A cross-border order names one of the eleven Incoterms 2020 rules and its named place, which decide who pays and carries the risk of each leg. The supply-chain function owns it, and only the supply-chain agent (role supply-chain-agent) or a person writes it. A purchase order commits money, so its writes carry decision class spend-money: an agent's write is held as a draft until a person accepts it, and sending it to the supplier is a person's act.

id.description: The order's id, the file name without .json, such as po-2026-001

supplier.description: The supplier by reference: the id of a supplier record (supply-chain/suppliers/<id>.json)

item.description: What is ordered: a SKU, part number or description

unit.description: The unit of measure, such as each, kg or carton

unit_price.description: Price per unit in the order's currency

total.description: The sum of quantity times unit price over the lines, before freight and duty

incoterm.description: The Incoterms 2020 rule; required in practice for a cross-border order

named_place.description: The place the Incoterms rule names, such as the port or warehouse

delivery_date.description: The date the supplier confirmed for delivery

payment_terms.description: Such as 30% deposit, 70% before shipment, or net 30

status.description: draft until a person approves the spend; sent and confirmed follow the supplier; received when goods arrive; closed when paid and matched

decision.description: The id of the decision record in which a person approved the spend
